item.title: Object ideals and idempotent completeness
item.description: arXiv:2611.07505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an idempotent complete Frobenius exact category with an idempotent complete stable category in which a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals induces a cotorsion pair of objects that fails to be complete. This gives a negative answer to the question of Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas under idempotent completeness. The construction uses a lemma on dense triangulated subcategories and an example of Bondarko and Sosnilo in which a weight structure fails to extend to the idempotent completion. The induced cotorsion pair is hereditary, and every object admits an ordinary precover from its left class and an ordinary preenvelope into its right class. We characterize which objects admit special precovers and which admit special preenvelopes.
item.dc:creator: Jing He, Yixia Zhang

item.title: Presenting Point-Glued Self-Similar Objects as Final Coalgebras in Metric Spaces via Completion: A Categorical Hutchinson Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.07584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study self-similar spaces obtained by repeatedly gluing finitely many scaled copies of a pointed metric space along prescribed boundary points. A finite gluing specification defines endofunctors on suitable categories of pointed sets and pointed metric spaces. Under non-degeneracy and metric admissibility assumptions, the initial algebra of the set functor carries a canonical metric. Its Cauchy completion is a final coalgebra for the metric functor and, after forgetting the metric, also for the underlying set functor. We compare this construction with Iterated Function Systems. When the orbit algebra is injective and its comparison with the initial algebra is bi-Lipschitz, the attractor is isomorphic to the completed final coalgebra. This gives a categorical analogue of Hutchinson's theorem for overlaps captured by finitely many distinguished points. Examples include the unit interval, Cantor spaces, the Sierpi\'nski gasket and $p$-adic integers.
item.dc:creator: Jayampathy Ratnayake, Annanthakrishna Manokaran

item.title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$. More generally, for gradings in any complete decomposition space $M$ with indecomposable identities, the terminal object is $J(M)$, the free decomposition space on the nondegenerate simplices of $M$; the quasisymmetric case is $Q=J(B\mathbb{N})$.
item.dc:creator: Philip Hackney, Joachim Kock, Jan Steinebrunner

item.title: Categorified convergence: dropping the 'ultra' from 'virtual ultracategories'
item.description: arXiv:2611.08124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Virtual ultracategories are a recent categorification of topological spaces seen as sets of points together with a convergence relation between points and ultrafilters. However, a topology can also be described in terms of convergence of filters: in this paper, we thus introduce an analogue of virtual ultracategories based on filters rather than ultrafilters. At the topological level, convergence of filters is completely determined by its restriction to ultrafilters. Our main result shows that, under the assumption of tautness, the same phenomenon holds at the categorified level, thereby offering a non-ultra-biased perspective on virtual ultracategories.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Saadia, Umberto Tarantino

item.title: A Complete Equational Theory for Quantum Circuits with Generalized Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.07207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Controlled subcircuits are commonplace in quantum algorithms as they represent the quantum analogue of branching statements (if then). We introduce a generalization of controlled subcircuits in the form of a binary operation which sends pairs of unitary quantum circuits to a generalized controlled operation, whose semantics are based on matrix exponentials and logarithms. The family of quantum circuits with generalized controlled operations and circuit exponentiation is denoted HQC for Hierarchical Quantum Circuits. We formalize HQC as a modified prop category using a novel category-theoretic construction, and provide a sound and complete equational theory for diagrammatic reasoning in HQC.
item.dc:creator: William Schober (Universit\`a della Svizzera italiana), Scott Wesley (Dalhousie University)

item.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.07262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.
item.dc:creator: Hisato Matsukawa

item.title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.07927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.
item.dc:creator: Lior Yanovski

item.title: Weak representability of actions of non-associative algebras
item.description: arXiv:2306.02812v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the categorical-algebraic condition that internal actions are weakly representable (WRA) in the context of varieties of (non-associative) algebras over a field. Our first aim is to give a complete characterization of action accessible, operadic quadratic varieties of non-associative algebras which satisfy an identity of degree two and to study the representability of actions for them. Here we prove that the varieties of two-step nilpotent (anti-)commutative algebras are weakly action representable, and we explain that the condition (WRA) is closely connected to the existence of a so-called strong amalgam. Our second aim is to work towards the construction, still within the context of algebras over a field, of a weakly representing object $\mathcal{E}(X)$ for the actions on (or split extensions of) an object $X$. We actually obtain a partial algebra $\mathcal{E}(X)$, which we call external weak actor of $X$, together with a monomorphism of functors ${\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X) \rightarrowtail \mathrm{Hom}(U(-),\mathcal{E}(X))}$, which we study in detail in the case of quadratic varieties. Furthermore, the relations between the construction of the universal strict general actor $USGA(X)$ and that of $\mathcal{E}(X)$ are described in detail. We end with some open questions. This version is preceded by a corrigendum. Theorem 2.11 of the published article, which states that the variety of commutative associative algebras is weakly action representable, is false: we exhibit a $16$-dimensional algebra $X$ with zero multiplication for which the functor $\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X)$ admits no weak representation. Hence this variety is action accessible but not weakly action representable. The corrigendum amends the statements affected by this error, corrects Proposition 2.8, whose "if" part needs a strong amalgam, updates the definition of partial algebra, and lists some further minor corrections.
item.dc:creator: Jose Brox, Xabier Garc\'ia-Mart\'inez, Manuel Mancini, Tim Van der Linden, Corentin Vienne

item.title: Composing Double Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.41551v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many kinds of generalised syntax, including internal categories, T-categories or polynomial monads, arise as monads in bicategories of a certain flavour: maps are some kind of span, and composition is some kind of pullback. We explain the pattern behind these similarities: each bicategory is stitched together from two simpler pieces by a distributive law, where the distributivity is governed by pullback. A key novelty is in the kind of distributive law we consider; where Rosebrugh and Wood considered distributive laws between categories, we instead consider pseudo-distributive laws between double categories. A key construction, drawing on work of Weber, obtains such a distributive law from a so-called co-crossed double category: one whose codomain functor is a fibration, and whose cartesian cells are stable under horizontal composition. We show the horizontal Kleisli double category of a monad T is co-crossed just when T is cartesian, and that the composite double category recovers T-spans; that the double category associated to an identity-on-objects functor is co-crossed just when that functor is a calibration in the sense of B\'enabou; and that Street's calibrated bicategories yield co-crossed double categories in a similar manner, recovering the double category of polynomials of Gambino--Kock.
item.dc:creator: Mitchell Buckley, Richard Garner

item.title: Higher path groupoids and the holonomy of formal power series connections
item.description: arXiv:2506.23880v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Building on ideas of Kohno, we develop a framework for the construction of higher holonomy functors via the transport of formal power series connections. Using these techniques, we obtain functors from the path groupoid, the path 2-groupoid, and the path 3-groupoid of a manifold. We show that the resulting higher holonomy functors can detect non-trivial classes in higher homotopy groups. As an application, we construct a Gray functor from the path 3-groupoid of the configuration space of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geqslant 4$ and compute its restriction to 3-tracks with constant boundary when $n=4$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cellot

item.title: Morse flow categories as exit path categories
item.description: arXiv:2605.27112v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the topological flow category $\mathcal{M}$ arising from a Morse-Smale pair $(f,\xi)$ on a smooth closed manifold $X$ is equivalent, as an $\infty$-category, to Lurie's $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$ of exit paths in $X$ with respect to the stratification by the stable manifolds of $\xi$. The objects of $\mathcal{M}$ are the critical points of $f$, and for every pair of critical points, the space of morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$ between these is the space of possibly broken trajectories of $\xi$ connecting them; it can be identified up to homotopy with the space of unbroken ones. The latter maps naturally to the space of exit paths connecting these critical points; we prove this map to be a weak homotopy equivalence. Then, we combine these ingredients with several others to construct a zigzag of equivalences between the homotopy coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$, denoted $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, and $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$. The $n$-simplices of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$ are homotopy coherent diagrams of $n$ composable morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$; we introduce the notion of unbroken diagram, yielding an $\infty$-subcategory of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, which we refer to as the flow coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$. The simplices of the latter give rise to stratified maps out of a family of stratified cubes, into $X$. We organize this family into a functor from the category of finite ordered sequences of critical points, to the category of $A$-stratified topological spaces, and we prove a comparison result with the usual stratified geometric realization functor. We finally use a theorem of Tanaka that associates a functor to a semi-simplicial map between $\infty$-categories that satisfies certain conditions. Our theorem has implications regarding constructible sheaves and the description of homotopy types in terms of flow categories.
item.dc:creator: Colin Fourel

item.title: A counterexamples to the Polishchuk--Van den Bergh conjecture on curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.10147v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct an effective $S_3$ action on the smooth projective model of $y^2=t^{12h-5}+t$ for every $h\geq1$. Its quotient has genus $h$, and the fixed quotient for the three-cycle class consists of two points. We prove that the derived category of these two points admits no $\bbC$-linear exact fully faithful embedding into the equivariant derived category. This gives a counterexample to Conjecture A of Polishchuk and Van den Bergh. More generally, for a positive-genus quotient we compute the maximum number of completely orthogonal exceptional objects as $\Sm_i\lfloor e_i/2\rfloor$, where $e_i$ are the inertia orders. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for conjugacy-class decompositions with embeddings linear over the quotient, and construct kernels on the natural fibre products. For genus-zero quotients we obtain Euler-form bounds and exact capacities for all-two ramification with at least four branch points and for types $(2,3,3)$, $(2,3,4)$ and $(2,3,5)$.
item.dc:creator: Shengyong Pan

item.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35534v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Bryce Virgin

item.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.05187v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Gordienko, Maria Morozova
